Design practice and teaching are the same job, done in two directions.

I have taught graphic design for close to two decades — foundation studies, typography, illustration, advertising technology, media planning and digital media — at Takoradi Technical University and the University of Education, Winneba in Ghana, and at Northern Illinois University in the United States.

Alongside that I wrote and designed two textbooks for Ghanaian students who had no affordable local one, sat on the four-person national team that wrote Ghana's graphic design and printing curriculum for the Ministry of Education, and ran production at a university press.

My research asks what happens when a design student's work is judged by cultural standards different from the ones that shaped it — a question that started in the studio and keeps sending me back to it.
